items.title: Reduce default virtual stick size to reclaim screen space
items.what: In the primary portrait gameplay view (e.g., the 'Qualifier' screen), the two virtual joysticks at the bottom are enormous, occupying roughly the bottom 35-40% of the vertical screen space. The 'Large controls' toggle in settings appears to be OFF by default, yet the controls are massive.
items.why: This pushes the fighters into the middle-upper third, making them appear smaller and reducing the visibility of the action. On a phone, UI elements of this size feel oppressive and waste valuable canvas that should be dedicated to the fight.
items.how: Scale down the default radius of the joystick components by 40-50%. They should be thumb-sized, not palm-sized. Keep the 'Large controls' toggle for accessibility, but make the default layout much more compact to let the fighters breathe.

items.title: Increase visibility of the loading progress bar
items.what: On the boot/loading screen, the progress bar is a very thin, dark brown line against a black background. It is barely distinguishable from the surrounding darkness.
items.why: Players on slower mobile connections might think the game has frozen or failed to load, leading to early churn before the game even starts.
items.how: Change the progress bar fill color to the brand gold/yellow (matching the 'FIGHT' button) and increase its height (thickness) by 2x or 3x. Add a subtle glow to match the 'tungsten' aesthetic.

items.title: Remove or auto-hide the persistent control legend
items.what: A semi-transparent box labeled 'STANCE' and 'TECHNIQUE' with arrow mappings sits directly above the joysticks in the gameplay view, floating between the fighters' feet and the controls.
items.why: It creates visual clutter in the lower-middle of the screen, obscuring the floor and breaking the immersion of the dojo. The information is redundant once the player learns the twin-stick mechanics.
items.how: Make this legend fade out automatically after the first round or after 5 seconds of gameplay. Rely on the existing 'MOVES' button for reference if the player forgets.

items.title: Tighten camera framing to emphasize the fighters
items.what: In the portrait view, there is a significant amount of empty dojo wall/ceiling space above the fighters' heads. The fighters occupy the center but feel a bit small relative to the canvas, especially given the 'photoreal sprite' selling point.
items.why: Pushing the camera too far back diminishes the impact of the character art and makes the combat feel less intimate and impactful.
items.how: Move the camera forward on the Z-axis or lower the camera height slightly to crop out the top 15-20% of the dojo background, making the fighters fill the vertical center more aggressively.

items.title: Improve legibility of the Round/Mode indicator
items.what: The pill shape at the top left saying 'ROUND 1/5 · QUALIFIER' uses dark grey text on a dark background. It is the hardest text to read on the entire HUD.
items.why: It provides critical context (how far along the player is in the career mode) but is visually recessive. Players might miss which round they are on.
items.how: Change the text color to the warm gold/white used in the main HUD titles (like 'QUALIFIER' in the center), or lighten the background of the pill to provide better contrast against the dark dojo.
